reference: Bash type/help define metadata expectations. Future operations need util-linux 2.41 fstrim and a reviewed closed filesystem/FITRIM syscall mock in a disposable VM. No trim operation parity result is claimed.
coverage: Bash metadata confirms that fstrim is registered as a builtin.
Bash help metadata contains the documented synopsis, table modes and dry-run description.
Deferred: -I colon-list selection, regular/non-empty file handling, fstab parsing and mountpoint eligibility.
Deferred: -a mountinfo parsing and local writable filesystem selection.
Deferred: -A fstab selection, device-tag resolution and root-device guessing.
Deferred: duplicate target/source handling, octal path escapes and positive/negative -t filters.
Deferred: -o/-l/-m size parsing, boundary values, option parsing and usage errors.
Deferred: FITRIM request values, verbose byte reporting, unsupported errors and aggregate statuses.
Deferred: single-target path validation and filesystem handle lifecycle.
exclusions: No fstrim operation is invoked, including dry-run mode; operation execution is outside this runner's authorized safety scope.

There are no GNU parity cases in this run. Operation comparisons require a disposable VM or reviewed syscall mock that supplies private mount tables, filesystem metadata and device/sysfs fixtures, and prevents every FITRIM request from reaching the kernel.
No real mount, device, filesystem trim, host mount-table inspection or privilege-dependent behavior is exercised.

cases.purpose: Check the Bash type contract for the loadable by querying metadata only; do not call fstrim.
Check Bash help metadata against the documented synopsis, -a/-A/-I modes and dry-run description without invoking the operation.
cases.script:
help_text=$(help fstrim)
case $help_text in *'Discard unused blocks on a mounted filesystem.'*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
case $help_text in *'fstrim [options] <-A|-a|mount point>'*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
case $help_text in *'in the first non-empty file of a colon-separated fstab/mountinfo list;'*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
case $help_text in *'-n does everything apart from FITRIM.'*) ;; *) exit 1 ;; esac
printf 'fstrim help contract present\n'

cases.purpose: Compare -I colon-list choice, regular/non-empty file rules, fstab-shaped parsing, malformed rows and mountpoint eligibility.
Compare -a mountinfo parsing and selection of writable local filesystems, including read-only, pseudo, network and unmounted entries.
Compare -A fstab behavior, LABEL/UUID-style device resolution and root-device selection from a supplied command line or fake sysfs.
cases.reason: Remaining obligations: r1: Only the UUID= form yields a positive selected row. LABEL= positive selection and the PARTLABEL=/PARTUUID= forms are not exercised.; r2: Root-device guessing is only inferred from duplicate-source deduplication; no selected row depends solely on resolving /dev/root.

cases.purpose: Compare duplicate target/source rules, octal escapes, repeated/trailing slash path equivalence, and case-insensitive positive and negated -t filters.
Compare -o/-l/-m size parsing (base-0 numbers, binary/decimal suffixes, fractions and limits), option permutation and representative usage failures.
Compare range arguments, verbose size formatting, unsupported-operation handling, quiet mode, and all-failed/partial-failed aggregate exit statuses.
Compare single-target directory checks, realpath/open failures, dry-run output and descriptor cleanup on success or failure.
